definitions.explanation: Describes something or someone that does not attract attention or is hard to notice. The negative form of {目立|めだ}つ (to stand out).

examples.japanese: {目立|めだ}たない⟦{色|いろ}→色：00849_iro⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{服|ふく}→服：00695_fuku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{選|えら}んだ→選ぶ：00835_erabu⟧。
examples.english: I chose clothes in an inconspicuous color.

examples.japanese: ⟦{傷|きず}→傷：02201_kizu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{小|ちい}さくて→小さい：00025_chiisai⟧{目立|めだ}たない。
examples.english: The scratch is small and barely noticeable.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦クラス→クラス：01084_kurasu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{目立|めだ}たない⟦{存在|そんざい}→存在：03326_sonzai⟧だった。
examples.english: He was an inconspicuous presence in the class.

notes:
The negative form of ⟦{目立|めだ}つ→目立つ：02431_medatsu⟧ (to stand out), functioning as an independent adjective. While grammatically a verb negation, {目立|めだ}たない is commonly used as a standalone descriptor, much like an adjective.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目立|めだ}たない⟦{場所|ばしょ}→場所：00829_basho⟧: an inconspicuous spot
- {目立|めだ}たない⟦{存在|そんざい}→存在：03326_sonzai⟧: an unnoticeable presence
- {目立|めだ}たないよう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: so as not to stand out
- ⟦なるべく→なるべく：01281_narubeku⟧{目立|めだ}たない⟦ようにする→ようにする：10987_younisuru⟧: to try not to attract attention

USAGE:
Often used when someone deliberately tries to avoid attention, or when describing something that blends in. Can be either positive (subtle, tasteful) or negative (overlooked, ignored) depending on context.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{地味|じみ}→地味：01573_jimi⟧: plain, subdued — describes the quality itself, not just visibility
- ⟦{控|ひか}えめ→控えめ：17234_hikaeme⟧: modest, restrained — implies deliberate understatement
- ⟦{影|かげ}→影：02191_kage⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{薄|うす}い→薄い：00764_usui⟧: having a thin shadow — idiom for someone with a weak presence
